notes: Only packet 147_scan094 and the shared workflow/rules/notation were used. The original and both native halves were visually read line by line against C and H. All eleven created local crops were inspected. No OCR, external sources or TeX compilation was used.

All boxes use the original 1693 × 2358 coordinates. Eleven one-time unrotated crops were enlarged with LANCZOS to 2800 pixels wide (folio 2400), with autocontrast and mild UnsharpMask solely for legibility.
The top 46 is in the dark main ink and head position. The bottom-left 93 is much paler and smaller; no authorial attribution is inferred for it, and it remains marginal foliation.

The page generalizes the construction to an arbitrary subgraph, separately gives S-prime and a sigma-stable half-edge subset, and describes the chosen marked subset and a special one-vertex case. These are the source's statements; this reading does not claim to prove their validity.
The opening object is plain X-prime. Its neighbouring high stroke belongs to the preceding text line rather than being an independent hat. The visible prime is retained.

The abbreviations néc. with raised t, =, and st.ble are retained without expansion. The baseline point in néc. is visible and is absent from C's unpointed encoding. The bracketed S-prime de S datum is faint but present.

The doubtful cancelled les was reviewed on the local subgraph crop and resolved: l, e and s remain visible despite the strike. C's separate struck partie doubt remains. Added uncertainties on struck irréductibles and the cancelled A accent do not count as textual corrections of C.

Application origine is cancelled, and a distinct application is written above it as replacement. The first display retains the masculine induit ending, without supplying an e for grammatical agreement.

The low bars around S-prime before par l' are treated as ambiguous retracing/underlining. No old letter or cancelled expression is invented. Both witnesses have S-prime; the added uncertainty alone is not an error row against either.

The lower insertion is physically above the alpha line, but its curved leader enters after alpha in S and the comma, before et où on prend. H attaches it earlier, after ponctuel. The insertion's right-hand A accent is independently doubtful because it overlaps the descender from graphe.

The displays preserve the source's two written rows each. Their mathematical text, object order, labels, primes and alpha indices were checked visually. The short right tips in the maps are retained as rightward arrows; no extra decorations or reversed arrow are inferred.
The last two lines end in ad-hoc de, without completing the sentence or adding punctuation from an unseen following page.

H's page note is editorial. Its emph wrapper for quelconque corresponds to the source underline and is not counted as a textual disagreement. Different accent widths, operator wrappers and ordinary line wrapping are not independent errors.
No targeted proof check, independent re-proof, computation or formal certificate was performed in this first-reader pass.

For blind reading, three box bounds are slightly expanded beyond the existing inspected crops: opening y0=16 includes the topmost folio stroke, subset-data y1=980 gives the faint S-prime its full lower margin, and point-map y0=1950 includes the upper brace/accent strokes. No first-pass crop was repeated.
